items.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation — Emulating Charge and Discharge with a SPICE Model and a Bidirectional Power Supply
items.summary: This lecture explains how a lithium-ion battery emulator under development at Marutsu can take the place of a physical battery when testing a battery management system (BMS) or charger. A microcontroller runs a SPICE-derived battery model with two RC branches in real time. A bidirectional power supply uses the model to reproduce changes in terminal voltage as the battery’s state of charge and current history evolve. The lecture also explains how the emulator handles power flowing back from the charger.The final section examines a simulated load step from 0 to 5 A. The output voltage settles to within ±5 mV of the model prediction in about 150 µs. The lecture concludes by identifying which aspects of this response still need to be verified on the test bench.

items.title: リチウムイオン電池HILSの設計論 ― SPICEモデルで充放電を再現する双方向電源
items.summary: 電池HILSを題材に、実際の電池に代えて模擬電源をつなぎ、BMS（電池管理システム）や充電器を評価する仕組みを解説します。2段のRC回路を含むSPICE電池モデルをマイコン上でリアルタイムに計算し、充電率や電流の履歴に応じて端子電圧が変化する様子を再現します。充電時に電源側へ戻る電力の処理も取り上げます。最後に、負荷電流を0 Aから5 Aに変えたときのシミュレーション波形を読み解き、出力電圧が約150 µsでモデル値の±5 mV以内に落ち着く結果と、今後の実機試験で確認すべき点を示します。
